title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II

sources.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
Results from On-Board CSA-CP and CDM Sensor Readings During the Burning and Suppression of Solids II (BASS-II) Experiment in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)
Concurrent Flame Growth, Spread and Extinction over Composite Fabric Samples in Low Speed Purely Forced Flow in Microgravity
Correlation of Normal Gravity Mixed Convection Blowoff Limits with Microgravity Forced Flow Blowoff Limits
Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

key_findings: Materials in microgravity burn as well if not better than in normal gravity under identical conditions
Flame appearance, flame growth, and spread rates were determined in both the opposed and concurrent flow
fields.earth_applications: Improved spacecraft fire safety and understanding of combustion in space to avoid fires on future space missions

conditions.label: BASS-II microgravity combustion tests
evidence: Fuel samples were mounted inside a small wind tunnel which could impose airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s.

conditions.label: PMMA rod, low-oxygen blowoff tests
evidence: With no restrictors, the maximum flow velocity was ~55 cm/s, and with two restrictors this was reduced to ~35 cm/s.

conditions.label: Cotton-fiberglass fabric blend, varying oxygen and flow speed
evidence: Ambient oxygen was varied from 21% down to 16% and flow speed from 40 cm/s down to 1 cm/s.
The flow speed could be varied from 1 to 55 cm/s.

conditions.label: 2.2 cm cotton-fiberglass fabric blend, 21% O2, varying flow speed
evidence: A 2.2 cm wide sample in 18.7% O2 was first ignited at 10 cm/s flow. Flow speed was decreased to 2.2 cm/s incrementally after ignition.

conditions.label: Cast PMMA rods, ground tests
evidence: Cast polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) rods of diameters ranging from 0.635 cm to 3.81 cm were burned at oxygen concentrations ranging from 14 to 18% by volume.
The maximum flow rate was 165 SLPM (60.3 cm/s average tube speed).

conditions.label: PMMA rod, low-oxygen blowoff tests
evidence: Oxygen concentrations in the MSG working volume were varied during the testing from ambient ISS oxygen levels (~ 21% O2) down to ~14% O2

paper_findings.text: The CO versus CO2 followed a linear trend for some datasets, but not for all the different geometries of fuel and flow tested.
The majority of the tests had heat release rates well below 100 Watts.
The global equivalence ratio for the tests is estimated to be fuel rich: 1.3 on average using mass loss and oxygen consumption data.
The quenching speeds were found to be between 1 and 5 cm/s with higher speed in lower oxygen atmosphere.
Flames spread more slowly across the narrower samples, at lower flow velocities and at lower oxygen percentages.

For this thin fabric fuel in concurrent flow, flame spread rate is relatively large and the sample is not long enough to fine tune the flow speed during the one to two minutes of experimental run time.
The forced flow velocity where blowoff occurred was determined for each rod size and oxygen concentration.
Each boundary is approximately linear with flow, with the exception of the 14% oxygen data.
The estimate is good because the microgravity quenching boundary turns upward away from the blowoff line only for low-speed flows.
The minimum oxygen concentration for stable flames was 13.3% O2
Flame spread was not observed below 16.4 % O2 in opposed flow flame spread rods tests
The solid conduction ratio falls off as Peclet number is reduced
